title: Samsung researchers and colleagues from Hanbat National University extend OLED lifetime by tuning the surface potential of the electron-blocking layer
summary: Researchers from Korea's Hanbat National University, together with colleagues from the Samsung Advanced Institute of Technology (SAIT), have shown that tuning the electrical surface potential of a thin layer inside an OLED can reduce efficiency losses and extend the device lifetime. Using an electron-blocking layer (EBL) with an optimized negative "giant surface potential" (GSP), the researchers extended the device's LT95 lifetime by about 20%, from around 29 hours to 35 hours.

title: Researchers design flexible, metal-free TADF molecules for efficient orange-to-red OLEDs
summary: Researchers from Japan's University of Osaka, working with partners in Poland, Denmark and the UK, have developed metal-free orange-to-red TADF emitters that use through-space charge transfer (TSCT). Unlike earlier long-wavelength TSCT emitters, the new molecules are flexible and do not need a rigid structure to hold them in shape. OLED devices made with the new emitters glow at 598–624 nm and reach an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of up to 14.
